hero.label: Made for Inlet
hero.headline: I want to be the SDR who helps Inlet own legal AI timekeeping.
hero.subheadline: Inlet is solving a real, expensive problem that attorneys have lived with forever: billable hours lost to memory and manual entry. I've spent the last year doing exactly what this role demands, building pipeline from zero and figuring out what messaging moves buyers. I want to be the person who helps Sean and Adam take this from early traction to a category-defining company.

whyCompany.title: The pain is real, the urgency is high, and the window is now
whyCompany.body: Attorneys lose thousands in billable hours every year not because they don't work, but because manual timekeeping fails them. Inlet passively captures that work in the background, which means the pitch sells itself once the right person hears it. Competitors like Billables AI exist, but Inlet's legal-native approach and YC backing put it in a strong position to move fast and establish the standard.

whyCompany.title: Two-person YC team means the first SDR shapes everything
whyCompany.body: With only two employees and a product that's clearly past proof-of-concept, Inlet is at the exact moment where the right SDR doesn't just fill a quota, they help define what outbound looks like for the company. Every sequence I write and every call I run will directly inform how Inlet scales. That kind of ownership at 21 is exactly what I'm looking for.

whyCompany.title: I've done early-stage outbound before, and it worked
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai, I ran cold outreach from scratch using HubSpot and LinkedIn sequences and helped the company land 15 to 20 paying clients before the product was well known. That wasn't a playbook I followed; it was one I helped build. My most recent role at NextAfter deepened my understanding of B2B messaging and what actually moves decision-makers, which is exactly the muscle Inlet needs right now.

quote: Most SDR roles hand you a script and a quota. At Inlet, I'd be helping figure out what the script should be in the first place, and that's the version of this job I actually want.
